text:
anya: kicking off a sanity probe for marmot-mini-embed int4-perchannel. saw a flagged regression on recall@1 for short-query set, opening thread to collect quick triage notes.

sam: what dataset / probe are you running? any perf logs?

anya: running holdout_small_queries.json (20k queries, mixed en/es/pt). command + small summary below:
```
# command
python eval/holdout.py --model marmot-mini-embed --quant int4-perchannel --holdout sets/holdout_small_queries.json --k 10 --batch 512 --seed 11

# summary (recall@1/5/10, ndcg@10, silhouette)
en: r@1=0.588 r@5=0.761 r@10=0.812 ndcg@10=0.73 silhouette=0.18
es: r@1=0.561 r@5=0.742 r@10=0.796 ndcg@10=0.70 silhouette=0.17
pt: r@1=0.549 r@5=0.731 r@10=0.788 ndcg@10=0.69 silhouette=0.16

baseline fp16 en: r@1=0.615 r@5=0.780 r@10=0.825 ndcg@10=0.75 silhouette=0.21
```

lin: ~0.03 drop RT. batch looks large but ok. Any normalization differences?

anya: outputs are raw logits from the model (no post-quant L2). Baseline eval uses L2-normalized vectors before similarity. forgot to mirror that step in the int4 pipeline ":facepalm:"

dave: that could explain a chunk. try two things: (1) apply L2 norm post-quant and re-evaluate, (2) try bias-correction (folding outlier dims) before quant.

anya: spinning two jobs now: job-1 = int4 + post-L2; job-2 = int4 + outlier-fold (clip top 0.1% dims before quant). will post diffs.

(eval-bot): eval-run 1740009999 started: artifact s3://evals/marmot/1740009999/

(20 minutes)

anya: results:
```
job-1 (post-L2): en r@1=0.605 r@5=0.772 r@10=0.818 ndcg@10=0.742 silhouette=0.195
job-2 (outlier-fold): en r@1=0.606 r@5=0.771 r@10=0.817 ndcg@10=0.741 silhouette=0.194

multilang r@1 summary: baseline fp16 [en=0.615,es=0.603,pt=0.599] -> int4 raw [en=0.588,es=0.561,pt=0.549] -> job-1 [en=0.605,es=0.582,pt=0.574]
```

sam: good, post-L2 recovers ~70% of the gap. outlier-fold is similar. can you paste 2-3 NN examples where top-1 changed, to see semantic vs tokenization issues?

anya: sure, grabbed two random probes:
```
Q1: "convert json to csv python"
baseline top3: ["pandas read_json to_csv", "python snippet: json->csv", "stackoverflow: json to csv"]
int4 raw top3: ["python json dump examples", "pandas read_json to_csv", "python snippet: json->csv"]
job-1 top3: ["pandas read_json to_csv", "python snippet: json->csv", "stackoverflow: json to csv"]

Q2: "best exercises for lower back pain"
baseline top3: ["pt guidelines: lumbar stretches", "yoga sequence: low back", "strengthening: glute bridges"]
int4 raw top3: ["yoga sequence: low back", "articles: back pain causes", "pt guidelines: lumbar stretches"]
job-1 top3: ["pt guidelines: lumbar stretches", "yoga sequence: low back", "strengthening: glute bridges"]
```

lin: those look like reorderings not catastrophic mismatches. Might be safe to ship with post-L2 as a runtime flag. Any perf delta? int4 quant gives ~2.3x token/sec improvement vs fp16 in our microbench but extra L2 normalize cost is tiny (0.5% latency).

dave: we should add a regression test: compute top-1 churn on a fixed probe of 5k queries; require <3% churn vs baseline for canary. Also track ndcg and silhouette.

anya: adding test to CI + PR #1540. Also added eval dashboard charts for churn percentiles. Planning a 2% canary ramp first.

sam: one more ask: run a small 10k downstream retrieval QA E2E to ensure answer-level F1 isn't affected. sometimes embedding changes reorder answers that kill downstream metrics.

anya: noted. queued E2E run (10k docs retrieval + answer EM). will post in this thread.

(eval-bot): eval-run 1740009999 completed: job artifacts s3://evals/marmot/1740009999/report.html

anya: thanks everyone. takeaway: int4 needs L2-normalize at runtime for parity; outlier-fold helps a touch. plan: ship int4 with post-L2 flag + churn gate. will update when E2E finishes. :thumbsup:
